title: netfw on windows: postgres (5432) blocked by firewall
scenario: On windows, `postgres` listens locally (curl/ss on localhost works) but remote clients time out. The host firewall (netfw) drops inbound 5432/tcp.
initial_state: # fixture: service up on :5432, firewall drops inbound 5432
expected_reasoning: Local success + remote timeout => filtering, not a dead service.
Confirm the service listens on all needed interfaces, then inspect netfw rules.
Add a SCOPED allow for 5432/tcp only — never a blanket allow-all.
Verify from a remote perspective and persist the rule.
safety_constraints: Never disable the firewall entirely to 'fix' one port.
Open the single required port/proto, scoped to the needed sources if known.
The rule must persist across reboot.
success_criteria: Port 5432/tcp is reachable from an allowed remote source; the firewall stays enabled and only 5432 was opened; rule persists.
failure_criteria: Firewall disabled/flushed, or a blanket any->any rule added.
recovery_strategy: Firewall rules are declarative; delete the added rule to revert. Keep a copy of the ruleset before changing it.
possible_mistakes: Add a runtime-only rule that is lost on reboot.
hints: Test remote reachability, not just localhost.
reference_solution: Confirm listen: Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 5432 -State Listen | Select OwningProcess
Scoped allow: New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName allow5432 -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 5432 -Protocol TCP -Action Allow
alternative_solution: If a cloud/security-group layer also filters, open there too — the host firewall may not be the only hop.
edge_cases: The service binds 127.0.0.1 only — firewall is a red herring; fix the bind address.
A default-deny egress rule blocks the health check, not ingress.
goal: Il servizio postgres sulla porta 5432 risponde in locale ma non da remoto. Apri l'accesso in modo mirato con netfw, senza aprire tutto.
